claim: Sam68/KHDRBS1 is pivotal for DNA damage-stimulated NF-κB transactivation of anti-apoptotic genes.
source: Previously we reported that Src-associated-substrate-during-mitosis-of-68kDa (Sam68/KHDRBS1) is pivotal for DNA damage-stimulated NF-κB transactivation of anti-apoptotic genes (Fu et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fu et al., 2016

claim: Sam68 is critical for genotoxic stress-induced NF-κB activation in the γ-irradiated colon.
source: Here we show that Sam68 is critical for genotoxic stress-induced NF-κB activation in the γ-irradiated colon and animal and that Sam68-dependent NF-κB activation provides radioprotection to colon epithelium in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing diminished NF-κB activation in Sam68 knockout mice

claim: Sam68-dependent NF-κB activation provides radioprotection to colon epithelium in vivo.
source: Here we show that Sam68 is critical for genotoxic stress-induced NF-κB activation in the γ-irradiated colon and animal and that Sam68-dependent NF-κB activation provides radioprotection to colon epithelium in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing increased survival and reduced colon damage in Sam68-sufficient mice

claim: Sam68 deletion diminishes γ-irradiation-triggered PAR synthesis in colon epithelial cells.
source: Sam68 deletion diminishes γ-irradiation-triggered PAR synthesis and NF-κB activation in colon epithelial cells (CECs), thus hampering the expression of anti-apoptotic molecules in situ and facilitating CECs to undergo apoptosis in mice post whole-body γ-irradiation (WBIR).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and immunoblot data in Figure 1B-C

claim: Sam68 deletion diminishes γ-irradiation-triggered NF-κB activation in colon epithelial cells.
source: Sam68 deletion diminishes γ-irradiation-triggered PAR synthesis and NF-κB activation in colon epithelial cells (CECs), thus hampering the expression of anti-apoptotic molecules in situ and facilitating CECs to undergo apoptosis in mice post whole-body γ-irradiation (WBIR).
evidence: Supported by data showing reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation in Figure 1D-F

claim: Sam68 deletion hampers the expression of anti-apoptotic molecules in colon epithelial cells post whole-body γ-irradiation.
source: Sam68 deletion diminishes γ-irradiation-triggered PAR synthesis and NF-κB activation in colon epithelial cells (CECs), thus hampering the expression of anti-apoptotic molecules in situ and facilitating CECs to undergo apoptosis in mice post whole-body γ-irradiation (WBIR).

claim: Sam68 deletion facilitates colon epithelial cells to undergo apoptosis in mice post whole-body γ-irradiation.

claim: Sam68 knockout mice suffer more severe damage in the colon following whole-body γ-irradiation than control mice.

claim: Sam68 knockout mice succumb more rapidly from acute radiotoxicity than control mice following whole-body γ-irradiation.

claim: NF-κB plays a crucial function in inflammatory diseases and cancers.

claim: NF-κB signaling pathway plays an important role in cellular responses to various genotoxic stresses.

claim: WBIR-induced transcription of Bcl2l1 was substantially tempered in the γ-irradiated Khdrbs1−/− colon tissue.

claim: The balance between severe DNA damage-triggered programmed cell death and genotoxic stress-induced NF-κB-mediated anti-apoptotic transcription is pivotal for cell fate determination in cellular responses to DNA-damaging agents.

claim: Cleavage of Caspase-3 was barely detected in the colon tissue derived from Khdrbs1+/− mice at 8 hr post WBIR.

claim: Caspase-3 cleavage is one well-established biochemical hallmark for apoptosis.

claim: Caspase-3 cleavage was substantially augmented in the γ-irradiated Khdrbs1−/− colon.

claim: There is an inverse correlation between NF-κB-mediated anti-apoptotic gene expression and DNA damage-triggered apoptosis.

claim: The amount of apoptotic cells on the colon tissue sections from the mock-γ-irradiated animals was comparable, regardless of Sam68 presence.

evidence: Supported by TUNEL staining data shown in Figure 3C-D

claim: Sam68 deletion expedites CECs to undertake apoptosis in vivo in parallel to the substantially dampened NF-κB signaling and anti-apoptotic gene expression caused by genotoxic stress.
